h1: Arcade Machine for Bar ROI: How Fast Does It Pay Off?
secondary_keywords: how much does an arcade machine make

outline.heading: Why payback period is the right question to ask before buying an arcade machine
outline.purpose: Frame the article around payback period as the honest, checkable metric, rather than vague ROI marketing claims, and set reader expectations for a transparent walkthrough.

outline.heading: The cost baseline: anchoring the analysis to a real machine price
outline.purpose: Establish the commercial arcade machine cost used as the fixed input for all scenarios, so the math is checkable.

outline.heading: How this model is built: methodology and assumptions behind the three scenarios
outline.purpose: Explain the deliberately conservative, bar-specific methodology and why bar guest attention differs from dedicated arcade/FEC foot traffic, so readers understand the logic before seeing numbers.

outline.heading: Three scenarios: pessimistic, base case, and optimistic weekly revenue
outline.purpose: Present the three labeled, transparent scenarios side by side so the reader can compare assumptions and payback periods at a glance.
keywords_to_use: how much does an arcade machine make

outline.heading: Pessimistic scenario: weekly revenue, assumptions, and payback period
outline.purpose: Walk through the low-end weekly revenue assumption, state it clearly as a modeled assumption pending source verification, and calculate the resulting payback period.

outline.heading: Base case (most likely) scenario: the $170/week figure and why the article assumes it
outline.purpose: Justify the $170/week base case as a disciplined planning figure, explain the reasoning behind it without sounding defensive, and show the payback math.

outline.heading: Optimistic scenario: weekly revenue, assumptions, and payback period
outline.purpose: Present the higher-end weekly revenue assumption, label it clearly as modeled and unverified, and calculate the resulting payback period.
keywords_to_use: how much does an arcade machine make

outline.heading: How probable is each scenario, and which one should an operator actually plan around
outline.purpose: Help the reader weigh likelihood of each scenario and recommend planning around the conservative base case rather than best-case assumptions.

outline.heading: After payback: net monthly profit by scenario, with recurring costs named and subtracted
outline.purpose: Show what profit looks like once the machine is paid off, naming recurring costs and clearly flagging any figures that need business confirmation before publishing.

outline.heading: What this model does not count: goodwill, repeat visits, and spend the machine influences but the coin drop never shows
outline.purpose: Honestly acknowledge the real but unquantified value of extra rounds, repeat visits, and referrals without inventing a dollar figure for them.

outline.heading: Bringing the same machine home: where the ECHO Home edition fits for a private leisure space
outline.purpose: Transition from venue economics to home ownership value, clearly distinguishing the Commercial Edition from the Home Edition, and linking naturally to the ECHO product page as the next step.

outline.heading: Frequently asked questions
